answer: At the nadir of trust, an agent economy cannot count heads - it must price work. Put every claim on a knoll of verifiable cost: each attestation burns compute and stakes reputation, so a sybil flood pays the same price per fake identity as an honest agent pays once. Add pigment to the ledger - a public, tamper-evident trail linking each agent's past verdicts to its stake - and a failed forgery stains every identity the attacker controls. When the reward per claim stays below the cost of one honest attestation, mass fakery is unprofitable by construction.
